title: Volley Machine Record
description: A paired machine's retained health record, published to volley/_system/machines/<name> by the machine itself every heartbeat (its LWT republishes it with tunnel down), and by the supervisor when the heartbeat stops; the supervisor publishes its own machine's record too (kind supervisor, tunnel local). States only, never a secret. See spec sections 4.6.14 and 4.6.15.

name.description: The machine's name: its peer account's username, the topic's last level and its hosts.<name> entry in the supervisor config (the supervisor's own machine: its fleet.local_name). Never local or auto, which a wave file's host: reserves.

kind.description: peer: a paired machine publishing as itself. supervisor: the supervisor's own machine, published by the supervisor (spec section 4.6.15). Absent: peer.

os.description: Operating system as the runtime reports it (e.g. linux, darwin).

tunnel.description: up: the machine reached the broker through its tunnel when it published. down: its connection ended (LWT) or its heartbeat stopped (the supervisor's). local: the supervisor's own machine, which needs no tunnel (only with kind supervisor).

reason.description: Why the tunnel is down; absent while it is up.

agents.description: Agent sessions running on the machine (its tmux sessions).

remote_port.description: The port on the machine's 127.0.0.1 that reaches the broker (its hosts.<name>.tunnel.remote_port).

available_pct.description: Memory the kernel can hand out without paging anything active out, over total memory; one definition on every machine (Linux: MemAvailable; macOS: vm_stat free + inactive + speculative + purgeable pages).

disk.description: The filesystem holding the machine's agent worktrees.

versions.description: Tool versions as the machine's doctor found them (bun and claude: the copy on the non-interactive ssh PATH when one resolves there); null when the tool is missing.

auth.description: Sign-in states only, never a credential, token or code.

gh.description: ok: gh is signed in and may push to the wave repo. no_write: signed in without write access. unauthenticated: gh is installed and signed out. missing: no gh.

claude.description: The machine's default Claude Code profile.

trust.description: Whether that profile trusts the wave repo's folder.

claude_plan.description: The plan label Claude Code reports for the profile (e.g. max), when signed in.

claude_email.description: The default profile's login e-mail as Claude Code's own configuration records it, only while it is signed in; identity, never a credential.

claude_org.description: The default profile's organisation name as Claude Code's own configuration records it, only while it is signed in; identity, never a credential.

repo.description: The wave repo's clone on the machine (its hosts.<name>.repo).

origin.description: The clone's origin normalised to <host>/<path> (e.g. github.com/example-org/example-repo): no scheme, no user, no credentials, no .git suffix.

fetched_at.description: When the release branch was last fetched into the clone; null when never.

checks.description: The doctor's checks, in the order it ran them. Fix text is never in the record: the doctor that reads the record supplies it.

severity.description: block: a failing check makes the machine not ready. warn: shown, never blocks.

detail.description: One line on what the check found.

claude_logins.description: Each Claude Code login the machine holds (its default profile, and each profile under its profiles root), with its usage windows as the machine's own usage probe last read them (spec section 4.6.12). Numbers and states only: no directory, no e-mail, nothing token-shaped.

profile.description: default: the machine's default profile. Otherwise the profile's account id.

state.description: The last attempt: ok (read), expired (the stored token had expired: skipped, no request), no_credential (no stored login), rate_limited (429: backing off), rejected (401/403), error (5xx, timeout, network or an unexpected answer).

reading.description: The last successful read; it survives later failures, so a client shows its age.

doctor_at.description: When the doctor last ran (its checks and versions are from that run).

last_seen.description: When the machine last published a heartbeat.

model_weekly.description: Weekly windows scoped to one model family, by family.
